prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Code · Config options with long tokens (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Option" · longest unbreakable word 131px · one-line width 131px
  col 2: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 90px · one-line width 334px
  col 3: header "Example" · longest unbreakable word 537px · one-line width 537px
  col 4: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 501px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A reference/config-option table: readers look up one option by name and then check its default, see a realistic example value, and read what it does. It is scanned by row, not compared across rows, so row identity (the option key) must be findable instantly.","reading":"Vertical scan down column 1 to find the key, then a short rightward hop to Default/Example and finally the prose Description. Option and Default form the 'lookup' pair read together; Example and Description form the 'explanation' pair. Rows must read as units, so keys should not break and the long code tokens should not be shredded into unreadable fragments.","groups":["Option + Default: the identity/lookup pair, read together in one glance","Example + Description: the explanation pair, both wide and both needing generous width","Option alone must lead: it is the scan anchor and the only column whose values are all short, uniform identifiers"],"keep_intact":["Option keys (server.port, cache.ttlSeconds, auth.jwksUri) — the row's handle; 131px + 21px padding","Default values (8080, 300, —) — short, cheap to keep whole","The Example token is a single 537px unbreakable string: it can never be whole at 360px, so it must either be given a scrolling width or deliberately split"],"may_wrap":["Description — ordinary prose, wraps cleanly at any width and absorbs height","Default's rare long value (334px one-liner) can wrap rather than steal width from Option","Example may be split only if the design accepts scroll or a fragment; it should not be squeezed into a 60px sliver where it becomes noise"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [152, 72, 66, 69] · table 360×1497px · row heights [60, 176, 339, 222, 385, 315] · column headers wrapped 3/4 · tallest cell 16 lines · mid-word splits 41
Design r0B: widths [152, 111, 558, 220] · table 1042×405px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 106, 83, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 682px
Design r0C: widths [152, 96, 290, 190] · table 729×474px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 153, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 3 · OVERFLOWS the box by 369px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
